title: Review Queue
markdown:
**What it is:** A quality-control queue for incoming knowledge, facts, and information *before* the Executive starts relying on it.

**What it does:**

- List items awaiting review with their status (pending, approved, rejected, needs revision) and priority.
- Open any item to see its full content and where it came from.
- Approve, reject, or flag an item for revision — and attach corrections without changing the original.
- Bulk-approve everything pending, or a whole domain at once when you trust the source.

**How to use:**

1. Open **Knowledge base** in the sidebar and click **Review queue** at the top of the left-hand tree — the badge on both shows how many items are waiting.
2. On the **Review queue** tab, click **View** on an item to read it and see where it came from.
3. Decide:
   - **Approve** — the Executive can use it.
   - **Flag** — mark it *needs revision* as a reminder to follow up. A flagged item stays in use until you reject it.
   - **Reject** — keep it out; you can add a note saying why.
   - Use the priority dropdown (↓ Low / Normal / ↑ High) to order your queue.
4. To fix a detail instead of rejecting the whole item, open **View**, type in *Add a correction or clarification…* and click **Add**. Active corrections are given to the Executive alongside the item; toggle one to **Inactive** to retire it.
5. Trust a source? Click **Approve all pending**, or on the **All items** tab use **Approve all pending in *domain***.

**Where items come from:** playbook and failure-case files you add or edit in the Knowledge Base, and any domain you choose to **Curate** — curating holds that domain's built-in knowledge back from the Executive until you approve it (**Stop curating** releases it). Company documents you upload go straight to the Knowledge Base and don't appear here.

**Example:** you add a *discount-policy* playbook under finance. It shows up here as pending; open it, add the correction *"Discounts over 15% need CFO sign-off"*, then **Approve** — the Executive now uses the playbook with your correction attached.

*Tip: when you open a playbook or failure case in the Knowledge base, its review status shows under the filename, with **Approve** and **Flag** right there.*

*Note: approved and flagged items feed retrieval; pending and rejected ones are kept out. Editing an approved playbook flags it for re-review without taking it out of use.*
